newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ATHLETICS-BAILEY DENIES HE IS ANTI-AMERICAN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY DENIES HE IS ANTI-AMERICAN.

text.p: Canadian Olympic champion Donovan Bailey said on Sunday that his war of words with the United States had been fought on behalf of all non-U.S. athletes who won medals at last year's Olympics.
"I'm not anti-American, I live there," he said, after winning the 100 metres at the Rio de Janeiro Grand Prix, his first outdoor race this year.
"I just think there was a huge lack of respect for all the non-American athletes who won medals in Atlanta. Look at the case of (Irish swimmer) Michelle Smith," he said
"All those athletes were there doing their best but they didn't get recognition they deserved simply because they were not Americans.
"When I said that, I was speaking not just on behalf of myself, or on behalf of Canadians but on behalf of all the foreign athletes.
Bailey was involved in several exchanges earlier this year with the U.S. media after what he claimed was a lack of respect.
"I guess it's the ignorance of Americans not understanding that people are better than them. It's starting to become funny," Bailey told the Toronto Star in January.
In contrast, Bailey, on his second visit to Rio de Janeiro, could not find a bad word to say about Brazil. "This is a brilliant place. I could live in Brazil," he said.

Bailey, who broke the world record as he won the 100 metres at the Atlanta Olympics, faces Michael Johnson, winner of the 200 and 400 metres, over 150 metres on June 1 in Toronto in a race to find the so-called world's fastest man.
